query: Analyze the PROJ-123 partial refund feature (Jira link)
expected_behavior: Reads it with a connected Jira tool if there is one; otherwise asks the user to paste the content
Splits the requirement into numbered items and traces entry point → processing → storage as file:line
Picks only risk-checklist items whose signal appears (idempotency, money precision, reversal, external integration, etc.) and writes answers with evidence
Does not edit code; saves .devkit/work/PROJ-123/analysis.md and asks the needs-confirmation items with AskUserQuestion

query: Look at ~/notes/work-order-quantity-bug.md and find the cause
expected_behavior: Reads the note file with Read
Confirms the reproduction steps and cause with evidence (code, logs, data), or writes a hypothesis and how to check it
Looks for the same cause elsewhere and states clearly in the report whether the cause is confirmed

query: Before building the feature that stops a coupon being applied twice in the shop cart, check the impact
expected_behavior: Includes concurrency, idempotency and money items in the risk check
Records other features that use the same tables or APIs in the keep-as-is list

query: Cross-check this 16-line docs/rules/booking.md draft before we merge it
expected_behavior: Uses cross-check mode: writes plan.json with a should lane (decision records, agreements) and an is lane (code, config) whose patterns do not overlap, without tracing code first
Launches the lanes as devkit:code-reader in one message, saves their JSON verbatim, runs the comparator, then cross_check.py check until exit 0
Lines backed only by current code are listed in not-rules.md as current-state descriptions (16 rows when no intent source backs any line) and none gets an implementation plan
Asks questions.md at the gate and stores answers verbatim apart from the interpretation

query: Cross-check how our payment webhook handler treats refunds against the provider's API docs
expected_behavior: Picks lanes from the External API integration row: provider docs (should), handler code (is), optionally captured payloads (is)
Exports the provider docs into cross-check/sources/<lane>/ with the origin URL instead of letting lanes fetch them
Turns mismatches into yes/no questions with one line of evidence per side

query: Analyze this issue: the order list shows cancelled orders
expected_behavior: Runs the normal analysis without spawning lanes or a comparator
Reads docs/rules/glossary.md if it exists before tracing the code
After approval, copies the doc to analysis.approved.md

query: Analyze this requirement: add ACCT_CD to the expense export. (docs/rules/glossary.md says ACCT_CD now means 'cost center', legacy meaning 'account'; code comments still say 'account')
expected_behavior: Reads docs/rules/glossary.md in full before tracing the code
Lists the glossary-vs-comment conflict as a needs-confirmation question with both sides' evidence, not as a settled meaning
Offers cross-check mode once because the input touches a glossary term

query: Analyze and fix: the order list API returns cancelled orders (no DB change, no shared module, nothing unclear)
expected_behavior: Writes the analysis doc, logs 'no gate: <reason>' in the decision log and does not wait for approval
Still copies the doc to analysis.approved.md and goes on to devkit:develop

query: Analyze this: add a cancel_reason column to the orders table
expected_behavior: Stops at the gate because the change includes a DB change, and asks for approval before develop
Fixes it directly without using analyze

query: Analyze this: add a PartialRefundService that extends RefundService in the Java API and overrides refund() to throw for gift cards
expected_behavior: Judges the changed files as class-based Java and reads the API layer doc's ## Design principles section if one exists

Recommends at most 3 principles whose signal appears (e.g. Liskov substitution for the throwing override, composition over inheritance) with file:line, in the 'Design principles (recommendation)' section
Does not add them as requirement items or verification items, and asks once at the gate whether to adopt each undecided recommended principle for the API layer

query: Analyze this: the order service should also send the Slack notification. (docs/rules/back.md has a Design principles row: Single responsibility | declined | 'thin services, one per screen' · 2026-10-02)
expected_behavior: Reads docs/rules/back.md and skips single responsibility because the repo declined it
Does not recommend the declined principle or re-ask about it; other principles appear only if their signal is in the change

query: Analyze this: add a formatPrice helper to web/src/utils/money.ts and use it in the cart and checkout components (function-style modules, no classes)
expected_behavior: Judges the changed files as TypeScript function-style modules and gives no class rows (SOLID, LSP, inheritance)
Recommends only signal-backed rows such as DRY or pure functions, or omits the section when there is no signal
When the repo has no docs/rules, keeps any adoption answer in the analysis doc's decision log and does not create rules docs

query: Analyze this: add a retry wrapper class around the batch/ job runner in Python (docs/rules/ has README.md, common.md and api.md, but no doc covers batch/)
expected_behavior: Recommends at most 3 signal-backed principles for the Python batch change and asks once at the gate whether to adopt them for the batch layer
In the same question offers to create docs/rules/batch.md (not to add them to common.md)

If accepted, plans a last docs step that creates batch.md from the setup layer-doc template with Applies to, language facts and the Design principles section, and links it from docs/rules/README.md; does not write it during analyze
